key_insight: Machine learning can identify degradation mechanisms in simulated lead-free RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells, but reliable predictions depend on representative training data.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports post-fabrication fault diagnosis, while replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises simulated efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through improved fill factor.
method: Compare forward-prediction surrogates trained on factorial grids and Latin hypercube samples.
Classify six degradation mechanisms from temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit voltage.
evidence_signal: The diagnostic classifier achieved macro F₁ = 0.938 versus 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline; forward-prediction R² fell from 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independently sampled devices, while Latin hypercube training restored R² to 0.995.
watch_item: Diagnosis is simulation-based, and the classifier does not generalize to mechanism combinations absent from training.
paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
